project_description: A reusable planning board for choosing the best next build tasks before writing code.

sidebar.title: Reference Stack
sidebar.subtitle: Localhost sidebar
sidebar.note: Keep this page open while building. Use the sidebar to compare the current app, inspiration references, and the active Working TODO plan.

phases.name: Clarity And Direction
phases.description: Make the first build decisions clear before touching the product surface.

checklist.label: Define the real user
checklist.note: Write who uses the app, what they need first, and what they should ignore.
brief: This task prevents the project from becoming a collection of features. Before building, decide who the first version is for and what problem the page or app must solve for that person.
Approve this when the user and core use case are specific enough to guide UI choices. Disapprove it if the project already has a locked brief and this would slow down execution.

checklist.label: Choose the first screen
checklist.note: Decide what the user should see immediately when the app opens.
brief: The first screen controls the whole product feeling. Use this task to decide whether the app opens on a dashboard, checklist, calendar, canvas, table, or editor.
Approve this when the first screen is still ambiguous. Disapprove it when the first screen is already obvious from the project type or reference app.

phases.name: UI Build Pass
phases.description: Build only the interface that makes the product easier to understand and use.

checklist.label: Create paper-like task surface
checklist.note: Use clear cards, readable contrast, restrained color, and no blur-heavy UI.
brief: This task keeps the product grounded in the Studio Flow feeling: clear, tactile, readable, and operational instead of decorative.
Approve this when the current UI feels noisy, vague, or too SaaS-like. Disapprove it if the existing UI already has the correct visual foundation.

checklist.label: Add approval states
checklist.note: Let Osiris approve, disapprove, and copy selected tasks for Codex.
brief: Approval states turn the board into a decision layer. They help separate things we will build now from things we are parking for later.
Approve this when the project needs collaborative planning. Disapprove it for a simple one-off page where approvals are unnecessary.

phases.name: Later Parked Ideas
phases.description: Keep useful but non-urgent ideas visible without pulling focus from the MVP.

checklist.label: Park future integrations
checklist.note: Move cloud, login, sync, or automation ideas here until the local MVP works.
brief: This task protects the first version from becoming too wide. Future integrations can stay documented without turning into today's build work.
Approve this when the project is being distracted by later-stage ideas. Disapprove it if the integration is essential to the very first usable version.
